title: yeu inference speed up idea 16khz  - is if feasible?
body:
looking at ways to speed up Yeu inference without rebuilding the models.
Chat GPT suggests generate a 16kHz audio (should take a quarter of the time)
I was recently able to stepped up diffrythym x2 by switching to fp16
can the models work/be made to work with 16kHz audio?

are there any major stumbling blocks with this?
author: sujitvasanth

comments.body: As pointed out in the technical report, YuE generates 16kHz audio first and then uses a lightweight vocoder to upsample the audio to 44.1kHz.

> As pointed out in the technical report, YuE generates 16kHz audio first and then uses a lightweight vocoder to upsample the audio to 44.1kHz.

Thanks I saw this after I posted it...so no benefit with this,,,

No, this is an audio generation model.

But we plan to support melody conditioned audio generation (in abc format, abc <-> midi is possible).

Hi, thanks for the suggestion~  

But we've decided to keep it because this song is actually quite good. Also, as long as it's in Chinese, it works—it’s meant to showcase multilingual capabilities.  

A lot of Chinese rap borrows from other cultures anyway, e.g. American West Coast style, haha. Using a shamisen accompaniment for Chinese rap, on the other hand, gives it a unique flavor, showing that the model has learned to blend styles.

title: How to generate just music, no lyrics?
body:
I tried passing in an empty lyrics.txt and not passing in the --lyrics_txt argument.  Both give errors.

Is it possible to generate a song without lyrics/vocals?
author: SoftologyPro

comments.body:
You can provide session label with empty lyrics " ", e.g. a space. 

For genre.txt, you should remove the tags related to vocal.

For lyrics.txt, it will look something like this:
```
[verse]
 
[chorus]
 
[outro]
 
```

I am not sure about the musicality though. You need to play around with the prompt and find a stable one.

Or you can simply use the instrumental track in the output folder. Our model provides both vocal track and instrumental backing track.

We just checked. Using several `\n` to replace lyrics will get you non-vocal result. e.g.

```bash
[verse]




 
[chorus]




[chorus]




[outro]

```
